_note: THE BOUNCERS of chapter 4's zero-gravity rooms - entity `bounce`, the role table's
`bouncer`. Four of them across three levels, and every one in a level that sets
no_gravity.
THE ROLE TABLE IS WRONG ABOUT THIS ONE, and it is worth saying plainly because the port
nearly believed it. entity_roles.json calls a bouncer `a solid polygon surface that
THROWS THINGS OFF IT, 64x64, shape=3, static, non-sensor`. The geometry half is right.
The throwing is not: ETHCallback_bounce imparts no impulse to anything, ever. It checks
whether `speed` is set, injects the defaults if not, and calls linearMotion - which
moves the entity ITSELF. Whatever gets thrown off is only what any moving solid does to
what rests on it.
WHAT IT ACTUALLY IS: a slab of solid geometry floating gently in a weightless room. The
function that supplies its numbers is called setNoGravityLinearMotionProperties, and all
three bouncer levels are no_gravity levels, which is the whole story.
ETHCallback_bounce (bytes 353694..353862) calls linearMotion(thisEntity, vertical=true,
angle=0, startAngle=0). linearMotion (bytes 327527..328407) is:
angle  += unitsPerSecond(speed)
offset  = cos(angle) * stride * sign(speed)
pos     = originalPos + getScale() * rotateZ(angle_param) * (0, offset, 0)
with the angle wrapped by adding -2*PI once it passes 2*PI. `vertical` picks
(0, offset, 0) over (offset, 0, 0); ETHCallback_bounce passes true, so a bouncer bobs
UP AND DOWN. rotateZ is by the `angle` parameter, which is 0 here, so it turns nothing.
THE NUMBERS COME FROM THE BINARY, NOT FROM THE LEVELS, which is the reverse of every
other mover in this port. setNoGravityLinearMotionProperties (bytes 353522..353694)
writes speed = 1.2 and stride = 1.0 onto the entity, and NO `bounce` node in any level
carries a speed, a stride or a direction - all four were checked. So these are code
constants recorded as data, rather than data read from a node. Mover::OscillationFromNode
refuses a node without speed and stride for exactly that reason, and cannot be reused.
STimeManager::unitsPerSecond(speed) is speed * min(200, lastFrameElapsedMs) / 1000 *
m_factor. m_factor is 1 in normal play (the constructor sets 1f; setFactor drives pause
and isPaused is m_factor == 0), so the angle advances at 1.2 RADIANS PER SECOND and a
full bob takes 2*PI/1.2 = 5.24 s. The 200 ms floor on the frame is the original's guard
against a long frame throwing a platform across the room, and it is kept.
THE AMPLITUDE IS ONE PIXEL. stride is 1.0 and getScale() is 1 at the 480-tall reference
(SGlobalScale, the same factor zerog.json decodes), so a bouncer travels 1 px up and 1 px
down. It is decoration, and the port builds it anyway: the geometry is already solid and
already built, so the only honest alternative was to admit the role without the motion,
which is the mistake `torch` nearly shipped with light_wall.ent.
sign(speed) IS NOT MODELLED. Every placement in the game takes the injected +1.2 and
nothing in any level can make it negative, so the factor is always +1. It is recorded
here rather than written as code nothing can reach.
Measured by counting NODES, not grep lines - the mistake torch.json records. 4 `bounce`
nodes across 3 levels: level1c one, level6c two, level16c one. Every one of the three is
a no_gravity level (level1c to level18c).
Each node is a position, metadata/entity_name, a Sprite, a StaticBody2D and a
CollisionPolygon2D - so LevelBuilder already builds the solid, and these levels already
start and land. Admitting `bouncer` to Roles::Moves is what turns that static body
kinematic so it carries what stands on it while it bobs.
level1c and level6c play once this is built. level16c does NOT: it also places a
gravity_agent, which is the gravity_well role and is not built.
